summary: Spherical linear interpolation between quaternions a2 and a3 with factor a4 in [0,1], writing the result to a1 (x,y,z,w). Computes the dot product v7 = a2[0]*a3[0] + a2[2]*a3[2] + a2[1]*a3[1] + a2[3]*a3[3] and flips a3's sign (v14 = -1.0) when the dot is negative to take the shortest path. When 1.0 - |dot| <= 0.00000011920929 the quaternions are nearly parallel and the code falls back to linear interpolation weights v5 = 1 - a4 and v10 = a4; otherwise it computes theta = atan2(sqrt(1 - v8^2), v8) and the trig weights v5 = sin(theta*(1 - a4))/sin(theta), v10 = sin(theta*a4)/sin(theta). The final components are a1[i] = v5 * a2[i] + (v10 * v14) * a3[i]. All four output components are written unconditionally, so an external poke to the output does not persist.

local_names.v10: weight on quaternion B (t, or trig form)

operations.description: Compute the dot product v7 = a2[0]*a3[0] + a3[2]*a2[2] + a3[1]*a2[1] + a3[3]*a2[3].
Choose the shortest-path sign: v14 = -1.0 when v7 < 0.0, otherwise v14 = 1.0; then v8 = v14 * v7.

When 1.0 - v8 <= 0.00000011920929 the quaternions are nearly parallel: skip the trigonometric branch and use linear-interpolation weights v5 = 1.0 - a4 and v10 = a4 to avoid dividing by near-zero sin(theta).
Otherwise compute v9 = sqrt(1.0 - v8*v8), theta = atan2(v9, v8), v13 = 1.0 / v9, then the trig weights v5 = sin(theta * v5) * v13 and v10 = sin(theta * a4) * v13.
Return the output quaternion pointer a1.
